dinners.name: Cilantro Lime Chicken Bowls with Roasted Mini Peppers, Cucumber Salsa & Lime Crema
dinners.blurb: Chicken breasts marinated in lime, garlic and cilantro, roasted with sweet mini peppers and red onion, served over brown rice with a cucumber-tomato salsa, avocado and a lime yogurt crema. Chosen for the deal: Perdue boneless skinless chicken breasts, BOGO FREE, with BOGO mini sweet peppers and baby cucumbers.
dinners.warn: COOK ONCE, EAT TWICE: cook ALL ~4.5 lb of chicken, BOTH bags of peppers and ALL the rice. Set aside ~1.5 lb cooked chicken + half the peppers for Wednesday, and half the rice for Tuesday.
dinners.alt: Grilled cilantro lime chicken breasts garnished with cilantro and lime wedges

items: ~4.5 lb Perdue boneless skinless chicken breasts (BOGO)
3/4 cup finely chopped cilantro, plus more to garnish
2 bags mini sweet peppers, halved and seeded
3 cups dry brown rice (makes ~9 cups; half is Tuesday's)
Salsa: 1 pint cherry tomatoes (quartered), 3 baby cucumbers (diced), 3 scallions (sliced), 1/4 cup cilantro, juice of 1 lime, salt
Lime crema: 1 cup plain Greek yogurt + juice of 1 lime + pinch of salt, thinned with a splash of water
2 limes in wedges; hot sauce at the table

directions: MORNING (or up to 8 hr ahead): pound the thick end of each breast so they're even. In a gallon zip-top bag (or 2), combine the lime zest and juice, olive oil, 3/4 cup cilantro, garlic and salt. Add the chicken, coat it and refrigerate at least 1 hour, turning once.
Cook the brown rice, all 3 cups (stovetop or rice cooker, ~45 min hands-off). Half is for Tuesday.

Heat the oven to 425°F. Spread the chicken over 2 sheet pans with the peppers and onion (tossed in 2 Tbsp oil, salt and pepper) around the edges. Roast 18-22 min until the chicken reaches 165°F, then broil 2 min for char. (The recipe grills it ~5 min per side, which also works if you'd rather use a grill or grill pan in batches.)
While it roasts, make the salsa and lime crema.
Rest the chicken 5 min, squeeze lime over it and scatter cilantro on top. FOR WEDNESDAY: put ~1.5 lb cooked chicken and half the roasted peppers in a container and refrigerate. Slice the rest.
Build the bowls: rice, chicken, peppers and onion, salsa, avocado, a spoonful of crema. Hot sauce on the side.
Once the leftover rice cools, refrigerate half of it for Tuesday.
dinners.reuse: Hands ~1.5 lb cooked chicken + half the roasted peppers to Wed, and half the rice to Tue. Shares cilantro, limes, cucumbers and scallions with Tue, and cherry tomatoes + Greek yogurt with Wed.

dinners.name: Honey Garlic Salmon with Brown Rice, Smashed Cucumber Salad & Broccoli
dinners.blurb: Seared salmon finished in a sticky honey-soy-garlic glaze, served with Monday's brown rice, a cold, crunchy lime-sesame cucumber salad and steamed broccoli. Chosen for the deal: fresh salmon fillets, $10.99/lb.
dinners.alt: Honey garlic salmon fillets glazed in a sticky sauce in a skillet

items: 2.5 lb skinless salmon fillets, cut into 6-7 portions
Sauce: 2/3 cup honey, 5 Tbsp soy sauce, 2 1/2 Tbsp white vinegar, 3 large garlic cloves (minced)
Cucumber salad: 5 baby cucumbers, juice of 1 lime, 1 tsp toasted sesame oil, 1 tsp soy sauce, pinch of sugar, salt, a handful of cilantro, 1 scallion

directions: Take the salmon out 20 min before cooking. Pat it dry and season with salt and pepper.

Cucumber salad: smash the cucumbers with the flat of a knife, tear them into bite-size pieces and toss with salt. Let them sit 10 min, drain, then toss with the lime, sesame oil, soy, sugar, cilantro and scallion. Chill.
Whisk the honey, soy sauce, vinegar and garlic. Microwave the broccoli per the bag. Reheat the rice with a splash of water, covered.
Heat a little oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Work in 2 batches (or 2 pans), splitting the sauce. Sear the salmon 3-4 min until golden, flip and cook 2-3 min.
Pour in that batch's sauce and simmer ~1 min, spooning it over the fish, until it thickens slightly. If it thickens before the fish is done, add water a tablespoon at a time.
Serve over rice with the remaining sauce spooned on top. Finish with sesame seeds and scallions. Broccoli and cucumber salad on the side.
dinners.reuse: Rice comes from Mon. Uses Monday's cilantro, limes, baby cucumbers and scallions.

dinners.name: Baked Chicken Pesto Pasta with Spinach, Tomatoes & Roasted Peppers
dinners.blurb: Whole wheat penne in a pesto-Greek yogurt sauce with spinach, cherry tomatoes, Monday's roasted chicken and peppers, layered with mozzarella and baked until bubbly. No new protein: uses the second half of the Perdue BOGO chicken.
dinners.warn: No raw chicken tonight. Use the ~1.5 lb cooked chicken and roasted peppers saved Monday. Thaw the spinach overnight, or microwave it.
dinners.alt: Baked chicken pesto pasta with melted mozzarella and cherry tomatoes

ingredients.group: Full recipe (generous for 4, with lunch leftovers)
items: ~1.5 lb cooked chicken from Monday, cut into bite-size pieces (instead of searing raw chicken)
Half of Monday's roasted mini peppers, sliced (adaptation)
1 box (10 oz) frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed very dry
Red pepper flakes at the table (the recipe stirs in 1/4 tsp; here it goes on the side for the kids)

directions: Heat the oven to 375°F and spray a 9x13 dish.
Boil the penne in well-salted water until al dente. Save 1 cup of pasta water, drain and return the pasta to the pot.
Stir the pesto and Greek yogurt together until smooth, then mix in the squeezed spinach, breaking up clumps.
Toss the pesto mixture with the pasta, adding pasta water until it's slightly saucy. Fold in the chicken, peppers and tomatoes.
Spread half the pasta in the dish. Sprinkle with 1/2 cup mozzarella and half the basil, then add the rest of the pasta and top with the last 1/2 cup mozzarella.
Bake 20-25 min until the cheese melts and starts to turn golden (a few extra minutes since the chicken goes in cold). Top with the Parmesan and remaining basil and serve.
dinners.reuse: Second appearance of Monday's chicken and peppers, now a baked Italian pasta. Shares cherry tomatoes + Greek yogurt with Mon.

dinners.name: Oven Baked Pork Chops with Crispy Potatoes & Roasted Brussels Sprouts
dinners.blurb: Pork chops brushed with a sweet-savory ketchup, soy and Worcestershire glaze, baked over crispy baby potatoes and broiled until caramelized, with a second tray of roasted Brussels sprouts. Chosen for the deal: Publix lean boneless pork loin chops, BOGO FREE (and Brussels sprouts 2 for $5).
dinners.warn: Boneless chops cook faster than the recipe's bone-in ones. Pull them at 145°F.
dinners.alt: Caramelized baked pork chops on a tray with roasted baby potatoes

items: ~2.5 lb Publix lean boneless pork loin chops, about 1 inch thick (BOGO; freeze the extra pack)
2.5 lb baby potatoes, larger ones halved
2 packs Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved (added side)
3 Tbsp olive oil, salt, pepper; a splash of cider vinegar for the sprouts

directions: Heat the oven to 430°F. Toss the potatoes with 1 Tbsp oil, salt and pepper on sheet pan 1. Toss the sprouts with 2 Tbsp oil, salt and pepper, cut side down, on sheet pan 2. Put both pans in the oven for 15 min.
Mix the glaze ingredients. Brush both sides of the chops, keeping about a third of the glaze for basting.
Toss the potatoes and push them to the edges. Lay the chops in the middle of pan 1. Bake 10-12 min (the recipe says 15 for bone-in). Stir the sprouts.
Switch to a high broil with the rack ~8 inches from the heat. Take the sprouts out once they're browned and splash them with cider vinegar.
Flip the chops, spoon on the reserved glaze and broil 4-6 min until caramelized and 145°F inside. Brush the pan juices over the chops.
Rest 3 min. Serve the chops with the potatoes, sprouts and the pan juices.
dinners.reuse: Stand-alone night. Second BOGO pack of chops goes in the freezer for a future week.
